steps.title: Ask for one column
steps.prompt:
SELECT means 'ask for'. To see all the product names, you write SELECT name.
FROM products tells SQL which table to look in. In plain words: 'show me the names from the products table.'
Type it with the ghost help (the grey text turns coral, then green as you get it right):
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name FROM products;
hints: Start with the word SELECT.
The column we want is called name.
The table is called products and is named after FROM.
Write exactly: SELECT name FROM products;
steps.memory_trick: SELECT … FROM … = ask the table for…

steps.title: Two columns at once
steps.prompt:
One column was easy - let's ask for two. You list them after SELECT, separated by a comma.
Writing SELECT name, price means: 'show me the names AND the prices.'
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, price FROM products;
hints: Keep SELECT name and FROM products.
Add a comma, then the second column.
The second column is called price.
Write: SELECT name, price FROM products;
steps.memory_trick: A comma between columns = 'and also show me this'.

steps.title: Only the price
steps.prompt:
Say you only care about prices today. You don't have to take the whole table.
You ask for exactly the column you want - that's the whole trick of SELECT.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT price FROM products;
hints: The column names live between SELECT and FROM.
We want prices only.
It's a single word that starts with 'p'.
Write: SELECT price FROM products;
steps.memory_trick: You get back only what you ask for.

steps.title: Predict the output
steps.prompt:
Look at this query, and predict what you'll see: SELECT name FROM products;
It's like asking the librarian for one list. Visualise it before you answer.
steps.task: What will you see in the result?
hints: We asked for one column.
Which one? The one that holds names.
Look at the word after SELECT.
Answer: all the product names.
steps.memory_trick: The output is exactly the column you named.

steps.title: There is a pattern
steps.prompt:
Every query you write today has the same skeleton:
SELECT the things you want, FROM the table they live in.
Get used to that skeleton - every lesson from here builds on it.
steps.task: Which word comes after FROM in the query SELECT name FROM products; ?
hints: FROM points at the place to look.
It's the name of the table.
It sells spices, rugs and lanterns.
Answer: products.
